CGIMail.exe CGI program in Stalkerlab Mailers 1.1.2 allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files by specifying the file in the $Attach$ hidden form variable.

Floating point information leak in the context switch code for Linux 2.4.x only checks the MFH bit but does not verify the FPH owner, which allows local users to read register values of other processes by setting the MFH bit.

The radius daemon (radiusd) for GNU Radius 1.1, when compiled with the -enable-snmp option, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (server crash) via malformed SNMP messages containing an invalid OID.

WinGate 5.2.3 build 901 and 6.0 beta 2 build 942, and other versions such as 5.0.5, allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files from the root directory via a URL request to the wingate-internal directory.

WinGate 5.2.3 build 901 and 6.0 beta 2 build 942, and other versions such as 5.0.5, allows remote attackers to read arbitrary files via leading slash (//) characters in a URL request to the wingate-internal directory.

FreeS/WAN 1.x and 2.x, and other related products including superfreeswan 1.x, openswan 1.x before 1.0.6, openswan 2.x before 2.1.4, and strongSwan before 2.1.3, allows remote attackers to authenticate using spoofed PKCS#7 certificates in which a self-signed certificate identifies an alternate Certificate Authority (CA) and spoofed issuer and subject.

Openwave WAP gateway does not verify the fully qualified domain name URL with X.509 certificates from root certificate authorities, which allows remote attackers to spoof SSL certificates via a man-in-the-middle attack.
Buffer overflow in Enceladus Server Suite 3.9 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long CD (CWD) command.

Directory traversal vulnerability in Enceladus Server Suite 3.9 allows remote attackers to list arbitrary directories and possibly cause a denial of service via "@" (at) characters in a CD (CWD) command, such as (1) "@/....\", (2) "@@@/..c:\", or (3) "@/..@/..".

### Impact
An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the PowerShell and Cmd shell wrappers provided by the `CliInvoke.Specializations` package (the `PowershellProcessInvoker`/`CmdProcessInvoker` invokers, and the `UsePowerShell`/`UseCmd` middleware in v3 pre-release versions).

The wrappers re-run a caller-supplied target and arguments inside a shell command (`pwsh -Command ...` / `cmd /c ...`). In affected versions the wrapped command was delivered to the operating system as a single `ProcessStartInfo.Arguments` string. The OS command-line parser re-tokenizes that string before the shell parses it, so a double quote (`"`) in the target or arguments breaks OS-level quoting and lets the wrapped shell reassemble a second, unintended command. 

An attacker could exploit this to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the host process.

### Patches
The Specializations Packages now deliver the command via `ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList` (natively where supported, and polyfilled in older TFMs), so that the operating system passes argv verbatim and only the shell parses the command once. 

Upgrade to:
- **2.8.5** (2.8.x line)
- **2.9.4** (2.9.x line)
- **2.10.5** (2.10.x line)
- **3.0.0-beta.1** (3.x pre-release line)

### Workarounds
No complete workaround is available. Until upgraded:

- Reject or strip `"` from any target path or argument passed to the PowerShell/Cmd wrappers. On 2.2.0 – 2.9.2 and 3.0.0-alpha.1 – alpha.4, also reject shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&`, `$`, backtick, parentheses).
- Alternatively, bypass the wrappers for untrusted input and invoke the target process directly so that no second shell parse of the data occurs.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

cves.summary:
### Impact
An argument-injection vulnerability exists in the `CliInvoke`
package's runner factory: `RunnerProcessFactory` on the 2.x line and
`RunnerConfigurationFactory` on the 3.x line.

The factory joins the runner arguments, the caller's target, and the
caller's arguments into a single `ProcessStartInfo.Arguments` string and
hands it to the OS. The OS command-line parser re-tokenizes the string
before the runner sees it. A double quote (`"`) in the target or in any
argument closes the OS-level quoted region and lets the next character
enter argv as a separate element.

### Patches
Upgrade to:

- **2.8.5** (2.8.x line)
- **2.9.4** (2.9.x line)
- **2.10.5** (2.10.x line)
- **3.0.0-beta.2** (3.x pre-release line)

### Workarounds
No complete workaround is available. Until you can upgrade:

- Strip `"` from any target or argument before passing it to the
  factory. On shell runners, also strip `;`, `|`, `&`, `$`, backtick,
  and parentheses.
- Or bypass the factory entirely and build the `ProcessConfiguration`
  directly. Set `ArgumentList` explicitly to the argv you want the
  runner to receive.

These are partial mitigations. They shift the quoting problem to your
code.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')

cves.summary: SQL injection vulnerability in loginact.asp for Hummingbird CyberDOCS before 3.9 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands.
Sun ONE Application Server 7.0 for Windows 2000/XP does not log the complete URI of a long HTTP request, which could allow remote attackers to hide malicious activities.

Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the webapps-simple sample application for (1) Sun ONE Application Server 7.0 for Windows 2000/XP or (2) Sun Java System Web Server 6.1 allows remote attackers to insert arbitrary web script or HTML via an HTTP request that generates an "Invalid JSP file" error, which inserts the text in the resulting error message.

A vulnerability was determined in itsourcecode Pet Shop Management System 1.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the file admin_reject_completed.php. This manipulation of the argument ID causes sql injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

BEA WebLogic Server and WebLogic Express version 8.1 up to SP2, 7.0 up to SP4, and 6.1 up to SP6 may store the database username and password for an untargeted JDBC connection pool in plaintext in config.xml, which allows local users to gain privileges.

SQL injection vulnerability in the bblogin function in functions.php in PHP-Nuke 6.x through 7.2 allows remote attackers to bypass authentication and gain access by injecting base64-encoded SQL code into the user parameter.
ZoneAlarm Pro 4.5.538.001 and possibly other versions allows remote attackers to bypass e-mail protection via attachments whose names contain certain non-English characters.
Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Zaep AntiSpam 2.0 allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via double encoded slashes (%252F) in the key parameter.
Eudora 6.1 and 6.0.3 for Windows allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a deeply nested multipart MIME message.

lserver in SAP DB 7.3 and earlier uses the current working directory to find and execute the lserversrv program, which allows local users to gain privileges with a malicious lserversrv that is called from a directory that has a symlink to the lserver program.

The WP Mail Logging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.17.0 via the 'email_address' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to extract complete logged mail rows belonging to other users — including recipient addresses, message subjects, full message bodies, and any URLs contained therein — whose addresses happen to match the wildcard. Exploitation requires an administrator to process a personal-data export request for the attacker's email address via the standard WordPress privacy workflow, and the attacker's address must contain a LIKE wildcard character (such as an underscore) that matches at least one other user's address in the mail log.

The Smush  WordPress plugin before 4.3.4 does not restrict changes to a network-wide access setting to network administrators, allowing an administrator of a single site on a multisite network to change it for the entire network.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Gemini Labs Site Reviews site-reviews allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Site Reviews: from n/a through 8.3.4.

The OTP Login & Register Woocommerce WordPress plugin before 2.7.3 does not adequately limit one-time-password verification attempts, because the attempt limit is tracked against a value the client itself supplies and can change freely, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to bypass the limit and brute-force the short numeric login code to take over an account without its password.

The Product Delivery Date for WooCommerce  WordPress plugin before 3.3.2 does not perform a capability check before disclosing order details through its calendar view AJAX actions, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to view other customers' order information.

The Salon Booking System  WordPress plugin before 10.31.9 does not correctly verify the authenticity of REST API requests and discards WordPress core's nonce check for cookie-authenticated sessions across the whole REST API, allowing unauthenticated attackers who trick a logged-in administrator into clicking a crafted link to forge requests in that administrator's browser, up to creating a new administrator account.

The Salon Booking System  WordPress plugin before 10.31.9 does not properly check authorization before creating a booking and trusts a caller-supplied user identifier and booking status, allowing unauthenticated attackers to create bookings attributed to arbitrary users, overwrite those users' stored contact details, and mark bookings as paid or confirmed without any payment.

The WPeMatico RSS Feed Fetcher plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 2.9 This is due to the plugin removing WordPress's wp_filter_post_kses filter from content_save_pre immediately before calling wp_insert_post() with RSS feed content, whenever the campaign's last editor had the unfiltered_html capability — a flag the plugin sets automatically for every admin-saved campaign. Imported item content is taken raw from $item->get_content(), only entity-decoded, and stored verbatim in post_content. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers, who publish or compromise an RSS feed that an administrator has subscribed a WPeMatico campaign to, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected imported post.

The HivePress – Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'message' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.32 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the site administrator has enabled user listing submission, and the script executes in the victim's browser at the moment of successful login via the embedded form on the attacker's listing page.

The WSP MCP AI Agents Connector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Disclosure in versions up to, and including, 2.9.5. This is due to the wsp_get_posts MCP tool being registered with an empty capability requirement while the MCP endpoint's authenticate() method accepts any logged-in user, and the wsp_execute_get_posts() callback honouring a caller-supplied status=all argument that expands into a WP_Query over 'publish', 'draft', 'pending' and 'future' posts with no author or ownership filter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to read the titles, URLs, authors, categories, tags and 40-word excerpts of every unpublished (draft/pending/scheduled) post on the site.

The Premium Packages – Sell Digital Products Securely plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'note' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.2.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit bypasses tag-based filtering because the payload is stored as a hex-escaped sequence (e.g., \x3cimg onerror=...\x3e) that sanitize_textarea_field does not strip, and is only decoded back into a live HTML tag by stripcslashes() during admin rendering — after all sanitization has occurred.

The TranslatePress – Translate Multilingual sites with AI Translation plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the target site to allow unmoderated comment submission on at least one post and to have a secondary language configured — both conditions reflect TranslatePress's primary use case.

The HUSKY – Products Filter for WooCommerce Professional plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.5 via the 'woof_settings[woof_stat][server_options]' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract the external MySQL host, database name, username, and plaintext password stored in woof_settings[woof_stat][server_options] from the inline woof_tm_data script object on any public frontend filter page. This is only exploitable when an administrator has enabled the Statistics extension, saved external MySQL connection credentials, and enabled Turbo Mode — all supported, documented plugin configurations.

The HivePress – Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<custom user attribute slug> (e.g. hp_custom_link)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.32 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured a custom user attribute with a display_format template placing the %value% token inside an href, src, or style attribute context, which is a documented and expected use of the plugin's attribute display feature.

The Salon Booking System  WordPress plugin before 10.31.3 does not restrict several of its booking REST API routes to users with the appropriate capability, allowing any authenticated user such as a subscriber to read every customer's booking records, including their personal data.

The Visual Form Builder WordPress plugin through 3.1 does not perform an authorization check before displaying recent form submission data in a dashboard widget, allowing any authenticated user (Subscriber and above) to read other users' submitted contact information, including names, email addresses, form titles and timestamps.

The WP Compress – Instant Performance & Speed Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 7.25.00 The vulnerability exists because the `start_comms` dispatcher (`wps_ic_comms::start_comms`), hooked on every front-end request, gates access only by comparing the caller-supplied `apikey` parameter against the stored plugin API key with no WordPress capability check and no nonce verification, then passes the unvalidated `group`, `setting`, and `value` parameters directly to `change_setting()`, which writes them into the `WPS_IC_SETTINGS` option without an allow-list. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary permission keys into the plugin's settings, causing `wps_ic_users::checkAndAddCaps()` to grant any WordPress role — including Subscriber — the `manage_wpc_settings` capability and thereby achieve plugin-administrator-equivalent control over the plugin's optimization, CDN, and critical-CSS surfaces. The API key required to pass the authorization check can itself be obtained without authentication via the `wpc_send_critical_remote` nopriv AJAX action: when the external critical-CSS service returns an `apiResults` field, `initCritical()` echoes the stored plugin API key back to the caller in a `wp_send_json_success` response, completing the exploit chain entirely without a WordPress login.

The Sunshine Photo Cart – Client Photo Gallery & Photo Proofing for Photographers plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 3.7.4 via deserialization of untrusted input . This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, the attacker can store the malicious payload unauthenticated via the public favorites page and trigger deserialization by viewing any image in a non-viewable or private gallery.

The Photo Engine (Media Organizer & Lightroom) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 6.5.6 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to permanently delete arbitrary media attachments via wp_delete_attachment and upload new attachments to the site, actions that require the upload_files or edit_others_posts capabilities. A Subscriber-level user can obtain their own wplr_auth_token directly from the profile.php page source, because the admin screen guard in Meow_WPLR_Sync_Admin::__construct() is commented out, causing wp_localize_script to leak the token into every admin page view; this token can then be used from a cookie-less HTTP session to invoke destructive actions on the /?wplr-sync-api endpoint.

The MB Custom Post Types & Custom Taxonomies WordPress plugin before 2.12.2 does not perform a capability check or validate a nonce on its migration actions, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to trigger a one-way migration that creates published records and permanently deletes a companion MB Custom Post Types & Custom Taxonomies WordPress plugin before 2.12.2's entire post-type and taxonomy configuration.

A flaw was found in cifs-utils. This flaw allows an unprivileged local user to achieve privilege escalation. When a privileged service mounts a Common Internet File System (CIFS) share using a user-controlled credentials file, input values are not properly sanitized before being assembled into mount options. A local attacker can exploit this vulnerability to inject unauthorized mount options, allowing them to bypass permission checks and execute files with administrative (root) privileges.

The Mobile builder WordPress plugin through 1.4.2 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, allowing unauthenticated users to perform SQL injection attacks on sites that also run the WCFM Delivery add-on.
